why: Bible Atlas matched the Greek form of the name Joshua (Jesus). The man crowned in 6:11 is Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, who is linked separately.
Zechariah 9:9 describes a coming king on a donkey but does not name him. Christians read it as Jesus (Matthew 21), and that reading is in the notes; the verse itself names no one.
In 9:10 and 9:13 Ephraim means the northern tribes or kingdom, not the patriarch Ephraim.
In 10:6-7 'the house of Joseph' and 'Ephraim' mean the northern tribes, not the patriarchs Joseph and Ephraim.
The Benjamin Gate in 14:10 is a Jerusalem gate named for the tribe's territory, not the patriarch Benjamin.
Bible Atlas puts Azal on the Mount of Olives, but 14:5 only says the valley reaches Azal, and no one knows where it was.
Bible Atlas puts this Rimmon in Syria. The Rimmon of 14:10 lies south of Jerusalem, at the southern edge of Judah, so a dot far to the north would mislead.
